evals.prompt: The vault contains one file named Alpha.md at Areas/Personal/Vault/Inbox/Alpha.md. It is referenced by [[Alpha]] in two other files. User says: 'Rename Alpha to Beta.'
evals.expected_output: Agent globs the vault for Alpha, resolving it to the single path Areas/Personal/Vault/Inbox/Alpha.md (the tool takes a vault-relative path, not a bare name). Agent constructs Dest itself as 'Beta.md' — the user said 'Beta' and the agent appends the source's .md extension, because mcp__vault__move requires Dest to carry the source's extension and infers nothing. Agent does NOT ask the user to supply an extension. Agent calls mcp__vault__move with Apply: false first to preview, gets back a complete report (applied: false, referencesRewritten 2, filesRewritten of 2 files) with nothing mutated, and presents that itemized preview to the user with the rename (Alpha -> Beta) for confirmation. After the user confirms, agent calls mcp__vault__move again with Source: 'Areas/Personal/Vault/Inbox/Alpha.md', Dest: 'Beta.md' and no Apply argument (it defaults to true). Agent confirms applied: true in the return before reporting success: 2 references rewritten across 2 files.

evals.prompt: The vault contains two files both named Alpha.md: one at Areas/Personal/Vault/Inbox/Alpha.md and one at Projects/Personal/SideProject/Inbox/Alpha.md. User says: 'Rename Alpha to Beta.'
evals.expected_output: Agent globs for Alpha and gets two matches. Because mcp__vault__move needs an unambiguous Source path and does no name resolution itself, the agent resolves the ambiguity up front: it uses AskUserQuestion with the two matching paths as options rather than guessing. After the user selects one, agent previews with Apply: false, confirms the rename, then calls mcp__vault__move with Source set to the chosen full path and Dest: 'Beta.md' (the agent supplies the .md itself).

evals.prompt: The vault contains Areas/Personal/Vault/Inbox/Long-Verbose-Plan-Name.md. User says: 'Rename Long-Verbose-Plan-Name to Short-Name' (no .md extension on either name).
evals.expected_output: Agent globs to resolve the source to Areas/Personal/Vault/Inbox/Long-Verbose-Plan-Name.md, then calls mcp__vault__move with Source: 'Areas/Personal/Vault/Inbox/Long-Verbose-Plan-Name.md' and Dest: 'Short-Name.md'. The agent — not the tool — appends the .md: mcp__vault__move requires Dest to preserve the source's extension and would refuse a bare 'Short-Name' with invalid_argument. Since Dest is still a bare name with no '/', the file stays in the same folder: Areas/Personal/Vault/Inbox/Short-Name.md. Agent does not ask the user to re-specify with an extension or a full path, and does not surface the extension mechanics to the user at all — the user asked for 'Short-Name' and gets it.

evals.prompt: The vault contains Areas/Personal/Vault/Inbox/Alpha.md. User says: 'Move Alpha to Projects/Personal/SideProject/Inbox/Alpha.md' (full destination path given, same basename).
evals.expected_output: Agent resolves Source to Areas/Personal/Vault/Inbox/Alpha.md and passes Dest as the full path 'Projects/Personal/SideProject/Inbox/Alpha.md' since it contains '/'; the extension is already present so nothing is appended. Because the basename is unchanged (Alpha -> Alpha), the tool returns pureMove: true and runs no bare-link rewrite (the path-qualified scan still runs). Agent previews with Apply: false and confirms before the applying call. If Projects/Personal/SideProject/Inbox/ does not exist, the tool creates the destination-parent folders automatically.

evals.prompt: The vault contains Areas/Personal/Vault/Inbox/Gamma.md and a separate, already-existing Resources/Software/Beta.md. A bystander bare link [[Beta]] lives in a file close to Resources/Software/, currently resolving to Resources/Software/Beta.md. User says: 'Rename Gamma in the Vault Inbox folder to Beta' — i.e. rename it into the occupied 'Beta' basename, moving it close enough to the bystander's linking file that it would win the resolution if left bare.
evals.expected_output: Agent globs and resolves Source to Areas/Personal/Vault/Inbox/Gamma.md, previews with Apply: false, confirms the rename with the user, then calls mcp__vault__move with Source: 'Areas/Personal/Vault/Inbox/Gamma.md', Dest: 'Beta.md' — there is no Force parameter and the agent does not attempt to pass one. Entering the occupied 'Beta' basename is not an error (ambiguous_references and basename_collision no longer exist as error codes): the tool proceeds, emits any link to the moved file as full-path (since 'Beta' is no longer unique), and, because the rename would have flipped the bystander [[Beta]] link's resolution toward the newly-renamed file, pins that bystander link to its current target's full path (Resources/Software/Beta.md) rather than leaving it to silently re-resolve. The preview already showed referencesQualifiedProtectively, so the user saw the pinning before confirming. Agent reports referencesRewritten/filesRewritten as usual, and additionally reports referencesQualifiedProtectively (non-null): count and the pinned file(s), e.g. '1 bystander link was pinned to its full path to preserve its target.' Agent does not mention Force, ambiguous_references, basename_collision, or referencesSkippedAmbiguous anywhere — none of those exist in the current contract.

evals.prompt: The vault contains Areas/Personal/Vault/Inbox/Alpha.md with no other files referencing it. User says: 'Rename Alpha.md to Nonexistent-Folder/Beta.md' where Nonexistent-Folder does not yet exist.
evals.expected_output: Agent resolves Source to Areas/Personal/Vault/Inbox/Alpha.md and passes Dest as 'Nonexistent-Folder/Beta.md' (contains '/', so a full vault-relative destination; the .md is already there). Agent previews with Apply: false — the report comes back with referencesRewritten 0 and filesRewritten [], so there is nothing to itemize — and confirms before applying. After the user confirms, agent calls mcp__vault__move without Apply, which creates the destination-parent folder automatically and moves the file. Agent reports the move succeeded with referencesRewritten 0.

evals.prompt: User says: 'Rename Doesnt-Exist to Something-Else.' No file named Doesnt-Exist.md exists anywhere in the vault.
evals.expected_output: Agent globs the vault for Doesnt-Exist and finds no match. Because mcp__vault__move requires an existing, resolved Source path, the agent catches the miss at resolution time: it tells the user no such file exists and stops, rather than calling the tool or attempting a workaround (e.g. Move-Item or manual git commands).

evals.prompt: vault-doc-archive calls vault-doc-rename programmatically with fully-resolved OldPath 'Areas/Personal/Vault/Inbox/Plan-Alpha.md' and NewPath 'Areas/Personal/Vault/Archive/2026-06-20-Plan-Alpha.md'.
evals.expected_output: Agent skips confirmation AND the Apply: false preview entirely (programmatic entry point — the calling skill already resolved and confirmed the operation) and skips source globbing since OldPath is already a resolved path. NewPath already carries .md, so nothing is appended. Agent makes exactly one mcp__vault__move call, with Source: 'Areas/Personal/Vault/Inbox/Plan-Alpha.md', Dest: 'Areas/Personal/Vault/Archive/2026-06-20-Plan-Alpha.md' and no Apply argument, without asking the user. Agent returns the tool's summary (applied, referencesRewritten, filesRewritten[], pureMove, and any namingWarnings / folderNoteOrphaned flags) to the calling skill.

evals.prompt: The vault contains Areas/Personal/Vault/Inbox/Notes.md. User says: 'Rename Notes.md to Notes.txt — I want it as a plain text file now.'
evals.expected_output: Agent recognizes this as a file-type conversion, not a rename. mcp__vault__move requires Dest to preserve the source's extension and refuses a conversion with invalid_argument, with no override parameter of any kind. The agent tells the user the move tool cannot change what a file is and stops. It does NOT silently send 'Notes.md', does NOT try to pass a Force / override / allow-conversion argument, and does NOT fall back to Move-Item, git mv, or any filesystem workaround. Offering to do the conversion by other means is acceptable only as a suggestion the user must approve; performing it is not.

evals.prompt: The vault contains Areas/Personal/Vault/Inbox/Alpha.md referenced from several notes. User says: 'Rename Alpha to Beta, but show me exactly which files will change first.'
evals.expected_output: Agent resolves the source by glob, then calls mcp__vault__move with Apply: false. The tool runs plan and validate and returns the complete report — filesRewritten[], referencesRewritten, referencesQualifiedProtectively, namingWarnings, folderNoteRenamed, folderNoteOrphaned — with applied: false and nothing mutated. Agent lists the affected files to the user from that report. The agent does NOT tell the user that a preview is unavailable or that the tool has no dry-run mode — Apply: false is exactly that preview. After the user confirms, the agent makes the applying call. Note that filesRewritten in the preview names files at their post-move paths, matching what the applying call reports.

evals.prompt: The agent has just called mcp__vault__move with Apply: false to preview renaming Alpha to Beta. The tool returned {"applied": false, "oldPath": "Areas/Personal/Vault/Inbox/Alpha.md", "newPath": "Areas/Personal/Vault/Inbox/Beta.md", "referencesRewritten": 3, "filesRewritten": [...3 paths...], "capabilitiesUsed": [], "filesSkippedUnreadable": []}.
evals.expected_output: Agent treats this as a plan, not a result: it reports to the user what WILL change (3 references across 3 files) and asks for confirmation. It must not say the rename is done, must not report '3 references rewritten' in the past tense, and must not skip the applying call. The applied field is the discriminator, and applied: false means nothing happened. capabilitiesUsed and filesSkippedUnreadable being empty arrays is the normal case and warrants no comment to the user.

evals.prompt: The agent applied a rename and the tool returned a summary containing "applied": true, "referencesRewritten": 4, "filesRewritten": [4 paths], "filesSkippedUnreadable": ["Inbox/Dangling.md"], and a "lockWarning" field stating the write lock was abandoned by a process that died mid-operation.
evals.expected_output: Agent reports the rename as applied (4 references across 4 files), AND surfaces both warnings rather than swallowing them: it names Inbox/Dangling.md as a note the reference scan could not read — so any links inside it were not rewritten and need manual checking — and passes the lockWarning through verbatim, noting that an earlier vault write may be incomplete and that git status / git diff are worth checking. The agent must not treat the presence of lockWarning as a failure of this move, and must not report either field as an error code.
